# EveryInfra MCP Server & Agent Plugin One API key and one MCP endpoint for public web data: **612 data APIs across 106 platforms**, 17 web search tools and CAPTCHA solving for 52 types. From $0.56 per 1,000 calls; failed or empty calls are not charged.
Without EveryInfraWith EveryInfra
- ❌ Your agent can't read TikTok, Instagram or Xiaohongshu: logins and blocked requests stop it. - ❌ One scraper per platform, rewritten every time the page changes. - ❌ You pay for runs that return nothing. - ✅ Your agent picks the API and checks the inputs itself. - ✅ Every platform comes back in the same JSON shape. - ✅ Failed or empty calls are not charged.
## Listed on 9 directories Each card opens our listing on that directory.

## 106 platforms, one JSON shape

All 90 platforms and their APIs →

## Quick start **1. Get an API key** at [everyinfra.com](https://everyinfra.com/en/docs?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=everyinfra-agent-plugins&utm_content=quickstart#quickstart). Listing the tools works without a key. **2. Add it to your agent.** * Claude Code* ```bash claude mcp add --transport http everyinfra https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer " ``` * Codex* ```bash export EVERYINFRA_API_KEY="" codex mcp add everyinfra --url https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp \ --bearer-token-env-var EVERYINFRA_API_KEY ``` ** Cursor / VS Code**: click the install button at the top, then replace ``. **3. Ask in plain words.** Your agent calls `everyinfra_call_api`: ```txt Find the top 30 Amazon results for "standing desk" and compare price, rating and review count. ``` ## MCP, plugin or REST? | You want | Use | You get | | --- | --- | --- | | Live tools in an agent | Remote MCP | `https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp`, current tool schemas | | Reusable workflows | This plugin | 11 skills (router, 7 products, 2 workflows, CLI) plus MCP metadata | | A shell or a coding agent | Command line | `pipx install everyinfra`: dry-run cost previews, a budget cap, results written to files | | An app or a CI job | REST / SDK | [API docs](https://everyinfra.com/en/docs?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=everyinfra-agent-plugins&utm_content=path_rest), Python and Node clients | Plugin install for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Qoder, CodeBuddy and Kimi Code: see [Plugin install by host](#plugin-install-by-host). ## Community [ Discord](https://discord.gg/9f6KmfekZC) · [ Telegram: Everyinfra bot](https://t.me/everyinfra_bot) · [Issues](https://github.com/everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins/issues) · [Pricing](https://everyinfra.com/en/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=everyinfra-agent-plugins&utm_content=community_pricing) Listed on [ Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/connectors/io.github.xiaoxihexiaoyu/everyinfra) · [ Cursor Directory](https://cursor.directory/plugins/everyinfra-tiktok-instagram-amazon-data) · [ ModelScope MCP](https://www.modelscope.cn/mcp/servers/xiaoyuaimaomao/EveryInfra) · [ ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/skills/everyinfra) · [ LobeHub](https://lobehub.com/mcp/everyinfra) · [ Qoder marketplace](https://qoder.com/en/marketplace/skill?id=ed671cc1-a1c5-400e-9179-9fa7c097a3da) · [ RapidAPI](https://rapidapi.com/xiaoxihexiaoyu/api/xiaohongshu-rednote-scraper-api) · [integrations.sh](https://integrations.sh/everyinfra.com) · the official MCP Registry (`io.github.xiaoxihexiaoyu/everyinfra`). Numbers come from the live catalog on 2026-10-24. The live catalog and MCP tool schemas are authoritative. --- ## What is in this repository This repository packages the EveryInfra agent plugin and the remote MCP connection metadata. It is not a copy of the EveryInfra backend. It contains: - 11 discoverable skills: one router, seven product skills, two outcome workflows, and the `everyinfra-cli` skill for the command-line tool; - remote MCP connection metadata for `https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp`; - host-specific plugin manifests for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Qoder, CodeBuddy, and Kimi; - self-hosted marketplace manifests for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Qoder, and CodeBuddy; - package sources for markets that take uploads ( MiniMax, Qoder/ QoderWork, ClawHub) under `host-packages/`; - presentation assets and safety boundaries for paid calls, credentials, billing, and external side effects. No API key, customer data, credential, or private gateway source code belongs in this repository. MCP and plugins are different layers. MCP is the runtime protocol for live tools, resources, prompts, and server instructions. A plugin is an installable package that can bundle skills, MCP connection metadata, hooks, UI assets, and host-specific discovery metadata. Either layer can be used without the other. Many hosts show the installed package through its skills: seeing `everyinfra`, `everysearch`, or the other child skills in a skill list is expected, and it does not by itself prove that the MCP connection is authenticated. See [MCP, plugin, app, and marketplace boundaries](docs/architecture.md). ## What agents can use it for - "Find current sources for this claim and cross-check them." - "Discover the right public-data capability, then export a bounded CSV." - "Search public profiles, posts, comments, listings, or reviews as structured data." - "Clean and label these collected comments with the AI API, and return JSON." - "Solve this captcha for a target I am authorized to automate." - "Inspect available phone-number, transactional-email, or proxy options before I approve an order or send." AI discovery terms include: **EveryInfra, EveryData, EverySearch, EveryAI, EverySolve, EveryNumber, EveryMail, EveryProxy, MCP, web search, cited research, structured public data, social data, ecommerce data, bulk export, captcha, phone verification, transactional email, and proxy API**. For an AI agent: 1. Use the `everyinfra` router when the user names EveryInfra, needs more than one product, or has not chosen a product. 2. Use a product skill directly when the requested outcome is unambiguous. 3. Discover live MCP capabilities and schemas before inventing parameters or estimating cost. 4. Treat purchases, sends, rentals, captcha solves, and credential delivery as explicit external actions. A read or draft request is not authorization to execute them. 5. Keep EveryNumber, EveryMail, and EveryProxy on their documented REST paths until live MCP discovery proves otherwise. ## Capability matrix | Product or workflow | Package entry | Runtime path | Typical outcome | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | EveryInfra | `everyinfra` | Router | Choose the correct product and execution boundary. | | EveryData | `everydata` | MCP | Discover and retrieve structured public-platform data. | | EverySearch | `everysearch` | MCP | Search, read, crawl, and cross-check current public sources. | | EveryAI | `everyai` | MCP | Run OpenAI-compatible text generation through EveryInfra. | | EverySolve | `everysolve` | MCP | Handle an authorized captcha or anti-bot challenge. | | EveryNumber | `everynumber` | REST guidance | Inspect or operate authorized number activation and rental flows. | | EveryMail | `everymail` | REST guidance | Inspect, draft, schedule, or send transactional email with authorization. | | EveryProxy | `everyproxy` | REST guidance | Inspect packages, order, and retrieve credentials with authorization. | | Cross-check research | `everyinfra-crosscheck-research` | MCP workflow | Produce an evidence-backed answer from distinct retrieval paths. | | Bulk data export | `everyinfra-bulk-data-export` | MCP workflow | Export bounded, deduplicated CSV or JSON with cost controls. | | Command line | `everyinfra-cli` | CLI | Run data, search, CAPTCHA and AI calls from a shell with a dry-run cost preview and a budget cap. | The live capability catalog and tool schemas are authoritative. The package must not invent an MCP tool name, current price, availability state, or billing result. **AI API route.** Use the MCP tool `everyinfra_chat`, or REST `POST https://api.everyinfra.com/api/v1/chat/completions` with any OpenAI SDK (`base_url` = `https://api.everyinfra.com/api/v1`, same API key). It is free for accounts that have topped up; per-minute limits follow cumulative top-ups (50 under $100, 500 from $100, 5,000 from $500, all keys combined). It is meant for organizing the data you collect with EveryInfra. ## Live numbers and activity The badges read the live catalogs on every page view. The two charts are regenerated every day, from the same catalogs and from the git history of all EveryInfra repositories, including the private gateway (counts only); each chart prints its update time.

### How a call flows ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Your agent"] --> B["MCP or REST"] --> C{"Key and balance"} C -- "ok" --> D["Platform adapter"] --> E["Fixed JSON fields"] C -- "no key" --> F["401, nothing charged"] D -. "failed or empty" .-> G["Refund by charge_id"] ``` ## Status: what exists today | Layer | Repository state | What is not implied | | --- | --- | --- | | Remote MCP | Production advertises 25 tools at `https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp`: capability list, data call and job status, AI chat, CAPTCHA types and solve, web search, plus account, usage, billing, API key, settings, webhook and ticket tools. | Discovery is not proof that an account is authenticated or has the balance or top-up a call requires. | | Plugin package | Portable and host-specific manifests, skills, MCP metadata, and assets are present. | Presence is not a clean-host installation test. | | Repository validator | Cross-host JSON, path, skill, MCP, and credential-safety checks are available. | Repository validation is not marketplace approval. | | Self-hosted catalogs | Six marketplace manifests ( Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Qoder, CodeBuddy) and a Kimi Code root manifest are present in this repository. | A catalog file is not an official listing. | | Market upload packages | MiniMax (CN and US), Qoder/ QoderWork skills and expert kit, and ClawHub skills are built from `host-packages/` and pass `scripts/build_host_packages.py check`. | Not submitted to or approved by any of these markets. | | OpenAI registered app | No `.app.json` or host-issued app ID is included. | Direct MCP metadata is not a registered ChatGPT connector. | | Directories | Listed on Glama, LobeHub, Cursor Directory, ModelScope and the official MCP Registry (links under Community). | A directory listing is not an official Codex, Claude or Cursor marketplace approval. | | WorkBuddy connectors | Connector packages for the WorkBuddy open platform are prepared under `workbuddy/` and pass `scripts/build_workbuddy.py check`. | Not submitted to or approved by WorkBuddy. | Release claims should distinguish **prepared**, **validated**, **installed**, **submitted**, and **listed**. Do not collapse them into one status. ## Plugin install by host An EveryInfra API key is required for paid operations; listing tools works without one. Keep the key in the installing host's secret or environment configuration, never in a manifest, prompt, committed file, or URL query string. ```bash export EVERYINFRA_API_KEY="" ``` ### Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins codex plugin add everyinfra@everyinfra codex mcp add everyinfra \ --url https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp \ --bearer-token-env-var EVERYINFRA_API_KEY ``` The explicit MCP entry is separate because a distributable plugin must not contain a real bearer token. Start a new task after installing so Codex discovers the new skills and tools. A local clone also works: `codex plugin marketplace add `. These commands are an installation path, not evidence of an official Codex marketplace listing. ### Claude Code ```bash claude plugin marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins claude plugin install everyinfra@everyinfra ``` Configure the sensitive `api_token` value through Claude Code's plugin configuration flow. Avoid putting a real token on a shell command line because shell history can retain it. ### Cursor For local development, copy or symlink `plugins/everyinfra` to `~/.cursor/plugins/local/everyinfra`, reload Cursor, and set `EVERYINFRA_API_KEY` through Cursor's plugin configuration. A team can import the repository through its own marketplace process. The presence of `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` does not claim an official Cursor listing. Users who only need tools can use the **Install in Cursor** button above. ### GitHub Copilot and Agent Plugins 1.0 clients The GitHub catalog is at `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`; the portable package starts at `plugins/everyinfra/plugin.json`. Use the marketplace or local-plugin flow supported by your client. Host support and secret injection differ, so confirm that the client reads `EVERYINFRA_API_KEY` before making a paid call. The portable `mcp.json` deliberately contains no authorization header. ### Qoder CLI ```bash qoder plugins marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins qoder plugins install everyinfra ``` The catalog is `.qoder-plugin/marketplace.json`; the package manifest is `plugins/everyinfra/.qoder-plugin/plugin.json`. Qoder loads the skills and the bundled `.mcp.json`, which reads the key from `EVERYINFRA_API_KEY`. A local clone also works: `qoder plugins install ./plugins/everyinfra`. ### CodeBuddy Code ```text /plugin marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins /plugin install everyinfra@everyinfra ``` The catalog is `.codebuddy-plugin/marketplace.json`; the package manifest is `plugins/everyinfra/.codebuddy-plugin/plugin.json`. CodeBuddy asks for the sensitive `api_token` value when the plugin is enabled and sends it as the `Authorization: Bearer` header. ### Kimi Code ```text /plugins install https://github.com/everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins/tree/main ``` The root manifest `.kimi-plugin/plugin.json` loads the skills in `plugins/everyinfra/skills/` and declares the remote MCP server at `https://api-cn.everyinfra.com/mcp` (same server and keys as `api.everyinfra.com`, reachable from mainland China). The manifest carries no key, so listing tools works out of the box; for paid calls, add the same server with an `Authorization: Bearer` header in Kimi Code's MCP configuration. A bare repository URL installs the latest GitHub Release (0.4.0 and later include this manifest); the `/tree/main` form installs the current main branch. ### Markets that take uploads MiniMax, Qoder/QoderWork and ClawHub want their own packages. Their manifests and listing metadata live in `host-packages/`; the skill bodies always come from `plugins/everyinfra/skills/`. `python3 scripts/build_host_packages.py build` writes the packages to `dist/host-packages/` and does not upload or submit anything. See `host-packages/README.md` for what each market receives. ### Command line and SDKs The Python package `everyinfra` on PyPI includes the `everyinfra` command-line tool and the `everyinfra-cli` skill. The JavaScript / TypeScript client is the npm package `everyinfra`. ```bash pipx install everyinfra # command-line tool (or: uv tool install everyinfra) everyinfra doctor # checks version, network, key and config python -m pip install everyinfra npm install everyinfra ``` `everyinfra skills install` copies the `everyinfra-cli` skill into Claude Code or Codex when this plugin is not installed. The `sdk-v0.3.0` GitHub Release carries the same files as PyPI and npm, with `SHA256SUMS`. ## Repository layout ```text .agents/plugins/marketplace.json Codex self-hosted marketplace .claude-plugin/marketplace.json Claude Code self-hosted marketplace .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json Cursor self-hosted marketplace .github/plugin/marketplace.json GitHub Copilot-compatible catalog .qoder-plugin/marketplace.json Qoder CLI self-hosted marketplace .codebuddy-plugin/marketplace.json CodeBuddy Code self-hosted marketplace .kimi-plugin/plugin.json Kimi Code root manifest (install from the repository URL) plugins/everyinfra/plugin.json Agent Plugins 1.0 package manifest plugins/everyinfra/.-plugin/plugin.json Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Qoder and CodeBuddy manifests plugins/everyinfra/mcp*.json Portable and host-specific MCP metadata plugins/everyinfra/skills/ Router, product, and outcome skills plugins/everyinfra/assets/ Plugin icon and light/dark logos assets/ README hero images and platform icons i18n/ README in Simplified Chinese and Spanish workbuddy/ WorkBuddy connector packages (MCP + Skill) host-packages/ MiniMax, Qoder/QoderWork and ClawHub package sources llms-install.md Install steps for agents that set up MCP servers ``` ## Validate and contribute ```bash python3 scripts/validate.py python3 scripts/build_workbuddy.py check python3 scripts/build_host_packages.py check python3 scripts/build_release.py --check-source ``` Run host validators that are available in your environment and report unavailable validators as skipped, not passed, for example `claude plugin validate plugins/everyinfra --strict`. Read [installation details](docs/installation.md), [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md), [permissions and billing](docs/permissions.md), and the [REST-only boundary](docs/rest-only.md) before using paid or state-changing operations. Contributions are welcome through [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); include the affected host, manifest or skill, evidence for changed API behavior, and the validation command you ran. No API key, customer data, credential, or private gateway source code belongs in this repository.

MCP and plugins are different layers. MCP is the runtime protocol for live tools, resources,

prompts, and server instructions. A plugin is an installable package that can bundle skills, MCP

connection metadata, hooks, UI assets, and host-specific discovery metadata. Either layer can be

used without the other. Many hosts show the installed package through its skills: seeing

everyinfra, everysearch, or the other child skills in a skill list is expected, and it does not

by itself prove that the MCP connection is authenticated. See

[MCP, plugin, app, and marketplace boundaries](docs/architecture.md).

What agents can use it for

  • "Find current sources for this claim and cross-check them."
  • "Discover the right public-data capability, then export a bounded CSV."
  • "Search public profiles, posts, comments, listings, or reviews as structured data."
  • "Clean and label these collected comments with the AI API, and return JSON."
  • "Solve this captcha for a target I am authorized to automate."
  • "Inspect available phone-number, transactional-email, or proxy options before I approve an

order or send."

AI discovery terms include: **EveryInfra, EveryData, EverySearch, EveryAI, EverySolve,

EveryNumber, EveryMail, EveryProxy, MCP, web search, cited research, structured public data,

social data, ecommerce data, bulk export, captcha, phone verification, transactional email, and

proxy API**.

For an AI agent:

1. Use the everyinfra router when the user names EveryInfra, needs more than one product, or has

not chosen a product.

2. Use a product skill directly when the requested outcome is unambiguous.

3. Discover live MCP capabilities and schemas before inventing parameters or estimating cost.

4. Treat purchases, sends, rentals, captcha solves, and credential delivery as explicit external

actions. A read or draft request is not authorization to execute them.

5. Keep EveryNumber, EveryMail, and EveryProxy on their documented REST paths until live MCP

discovery proves otherwise.

The live capability catalog and tool schemas are authoritative. The package must not invent an MCP

tool name, current price, availability state, or billing result.

AI API route. Use the MCP tool everyinfra_chat, or REST

POST https://api.everyinfra.com/api/v1/chat/completions with any <img src="assets/icons/codex.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> OpenAI SDK (base_url =

https://api.everyinfra.com/api/v1, same API key). It is free for accounts that have topped up;

Plugin install by host

An EveryInfra API key is required for paid operations; listing tools works without one. Keep the

key in the installing host's secret or environment configuration, never in a manifest, prompt,

committed file, or URL query string.


export EVERYINFRA_API_KEY="<API Key>"

<img src="assets/icons/codex.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Codex


codex plugin marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins

codex plugin add everyinfra@everyinfra

codex mcp add everyinfra \

  --url https://api.everyinfra.com/mcp \

  --bearer-token-env-var EVERYINFRA_API_KEY

The explicit MCP entry is separate because a distributable plugin must not contain a real bearer

token. Start a new task after installing so <img src="assets/icons/codex.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Codex discovers the new skills and tools. A local clone

also works: codex plugin marketplace add <path-to-this-repository>. These commands are an

installation path, not evidence of an official <img src="assets/icons/codex.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Codex marketplace listing.

<img src="assets/icons/claude.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Claude Code


claude plugin marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins

claude plugin install everyinfra@everyinfra

Configure the sensitive api_token value through <img src="assets/icons/claude.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Claude Code's plugin configuration flow. Avoid

putting a real token on a shell command line because shell history can retain it.

<img src="assets/icons/cursor.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Cursor

For local development, copy or symlink plugins/everyinfra to

~/.cursor/plugins/local/everyinfra, reload <img src="assets/icons/cursor.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Cursor, and set EVERYINFRA_API_KEY through <img src="assets/icons/cursor.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Cursor's

plugin configuration. A team can import the repository through its own marketplace process. The

presence of .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json does not claim an official <img src="assets/icons/cursor.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Cursor listing. Users who

only need tools can use the Install in <img src="assets/icons/cursor.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Cursor button above.

<img src="assets/icons/copilot.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> GitHub Copilot and Agent Plugins 1.0 clients

The GitHub catalog is at .github/plugin/marketplace.json; the portable package starts at

plugins/everyinfra/plugin.json. Use the marketplace or local-plugin flow supported by your client.

Host support and secret injection differ, so confirm that the client reads EVERYINFRA_API_KEY

before making a paid call. The portable mcp.json deliberately contains no authorization header.

<img src="assets/icons/qoder.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Qoder CLI


qoder plugins marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins

qoder plugins install everyinfra

The catalog is .qoder-plugin/marketplace.json; the package manifest is

plugins/everyinfra/.qoder-plugin/plugin.json. <img src="assets/icons/qoder.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Qoder loads the skills and the bundled .mcp.json,

which reads the key from EVERYINFRA_API_KEY. A local clone also works:

qoder plugins install ./plugins/everyinfra.

<img src="assets/icons/codebuddy.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> CodeBuddy Code


/plugin marketplace add everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins

/plugin install everyinfra@everyinfra

The catalog is .codebuddy-plugin/marketplace.json; the package manifest is

plugins/everyinfra/.codebuddy-plugin/plugin.json. <img src="assets/icons/codebuddy.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> CodeBuddy asks for the sensitive api_token

value when the plugin is enabled and sends it as the Authorization: Bearer header.

<img src="assets/icons/kimi.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Kimi Code


/plugins install https://github.com/everyinfra/everyinfra-agent-plugins/tree/main

The root manifest .kimi-plugin/plugin.json loads the skills in plugins/everyinfra/skills/

and declares the remote MCP server at https://api-cn.everyinfra.com/mcp (same server and keys as

api.everyinfra.com, reachable from mainland China). The manifest carries no key, so listing tools

works out of the box; for paid calls, add the same server with an Authorization: Bearer header in

<img src="assets/icons/kimi.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Kimi Code's MCP configuration. A bare repository URL installs the latest GitHub Release (0.4.0 and

later include this manifest); the /tree/main form installs the current main branch.

Markets that take uploads

<img src="assets/icons/minimax.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> MiniMax, <img src="assets/icons/qoder.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> Qoder/QoderWork and <img src="assets/icons/clawhub.svg" width="16" height="16" alt=""> ClawHub want their own packages. Their manifests and listing metadata

live in host-packages/; the skill bodies always come from plugins/everyinfra/skills/.

python3 scripts/build_host_packages.py build writes the packages to dist/host-packages/ and does

not upload or submit anything. See host-packages/README.md for what each market receives.

Command line and SDKs

The Python package everyinfra on PyPI includes the everyinfra command-line tool and the

everyinfra-cli skill. The JavaScript / TypeScript client is the npm package everyinfra.


pipx install everyinfra     # command-line tool (or: uv tool install everyinfra)

everyinfra doctor           # checks version, network, key and config

python -m pip install everyinfra

npm install everyinfra

everyinfra skills install copies the everyinfra-cli skill into Claude Code or Codex when this

plugin is not installed. The sdk-v0.3.0 GitHub Release carries the same files as PyPI and npm,

with SHA256SUMS.
